why: V92Transmitter::reset and t_v92txreset.cpp were written by one hand from one reading of .text+0x53d10. About 2,000 of the function's 2,161 bytes are diagnostics, so the entries below split cleanly: the ones that change what reset WRITES or what it PASSES are killed at level 0 by the block comparison and by the sub-object comparison, and the ones that change a format string or an argument are killed only by the level-2 transcript run. WHAT NO ENTRY HERE CAN REACH: the ORDER of the six calls. The fixture compares the sub-objects after all six have run and none of the six reads what another wrote, so permuting them is invisible -- that rests on the disassembly and not on this tier.
